summary: Howan, the Rice Isle: a maritime commonwealth of terraces and one deep harbour, which keeps a house for the shipwrecked and may shelter a stranger.

rice_terraces.name: The Rice Terraces
rice_terraces.desc: Stepped paddies climb the hills in a hundred green tiers, each fed by the one above. Howan's villages open the sluices together at planting, and feast together at harvest.

speakers_house.name: The Speakers' House
speakers_house.desc: The Speakers are chosen by the terrace villages and the harbour guilds, and they meet in a long house above the quay. A Speaker holds office for three seasons and is never chosen twice running.

republic_of_howan.name: The Commonwealth of Howan
republic_of_howan.desc: Terrace and harbour have learned to share one table, and a quarrel between them is settled by the Speakers before supper. Howan is small, and it is steady.

western_trade.name: Trade With the West
western_trade.desc: Howan's rice goes north to the coast of the West Lands, and what it brings back is salt, tools and gossip. A ship that has called once calls again.

rescue_boats.name: The Rescue Boats
rescue_boats.desc: Two strong boats are kept ready at the mouth of the harbour, crewed by fishers who have pulled drowned men from the reef. They go out in any weather and ask no name.

harvest_festival.title: The Harvest Festival
harvest_festival.desc: The terraces are cut and the boats come for rice. The festival drums sound along the stairs of the hills, and the Speakers must say how much of the crop goes to the quay and how much to the granary.

focuses.name: Howan, the Rice Isle
focuses.desc: Howan is the westernmost of the southern isles, a rice island with stepped terraces and one deep harbour. Its Speaker, Tich Howa, presides over a quiet people who sell rice to every passing ship.

focuses.name: The Terraces of Howan
focuses.desc: Every hillside is cut into green steps, and every step is mended after the rains. The terrace-masters walk the stairs each dawn, tapping the walls with long wooden staves.

focuses.name: The Water Stairs
focuses.desc: Channels, sluices and stone aqueducts carry mountain water from step to step. The water-wardens count each drop, and have never been known to lose one.

focuses.name: Rice for the Ships
focuses.desc: A rice-market is set up on the quay, with scales, sacks and a bell to announce the price. Ships' cooks line up at dawn, and the market closes when the last sack is sold.

focuses.name: The Granary of the Isles
focuses.desc: Howan's granaries stand on stilts above the flood, and a seal is set on every door. In a bad season the other isles send boats to the quay, and nobody leaves empty.

focuses.name: The Harvest Festival
focuses.desc: The drums sound at the first cut, and the whole island climbs to the highest terrace for a feast. Even the harbour guilds are quiet for a night.

focuses.name: Rice Merchants
focuses.desc: A guild of rice merchants takes the sacks from the farmers and sells them to ships at a steady price. Their warehouse is the biggest building in the island.

focuses.name: The Speakers' House
focuses.desc: The long house above the quay seats a Speaker from every terrace village and every harbour guild. Their talk is slow, and their decisions stand for years.

focuses.name: Free Elections of Howan
focuses.desc: Every household may cast a pebble in the voting-jars at the quay. The jars are counted in public, and the smallest village has as loud a voice as the largest.

focuses.name: The Harbour Guilds
focuses.desc: Boatwrights, rope-makers and net-menders form their own guilds, each with a hall and a seal. The guilds send their wardens to the Speakers' House and are listened to.

focuses.name: The Commonwealth of Howan
focuses.desc: The terraces and the harbour are named one commonwealth under one seal, and the seal is carried in procession at midwinter. The island sets its name on every chart.

focuses.name: The Western Harbour
focuses.desc: The deep harbour is cleared of silt, its quay is extended and a second mole is begun. Ships from the west find Howan the first safe water after the storm seas.

focuses.name: Traders to the West
focuses.desc: Howan's merchants sail north to the West Lands coast with rice and return with iron and rope. The route is long and well worn, and each captain keeps his own chart.

focuses.name: Ships of Howan
focuses.desc: Shipwrights lay down a new yard beside the harbour, with a slipway for ocean hulls. Howan's boats are narrow and quick, and they ride the swell like gulls.

focuses.name: Hulls for the West
focuses.desc: The West is building a fleet for a crossing of the central sea, and has asked the isles for hulls. Howan's yards offer five, delivered and paid.

focuses.name: The House of Castaways
focuses.desc: Howan has kept a house for the shipwrecked for as long as there have been storms. A fire is never allowed to go out, and a bed is never allowed to be empty.

effects.tooltip: Howan has kept a house for the shipwrecked for as long as there have been storms.

focuses.name: The Rescue Boats
focuses.desc: The harbour fishers form a company of rescue boats, with oilskins, lines and a lantern for every thwart. They are paid only when they bring someone back.

focuses.name: A Seat by the Fire
focuses.desc: A stranger from the wreck is given dry clothes and a place at the hearth. He eats little, speaks softly, and asks the way to an old kingdom whose name the fishers have never heard.

effects.tooltip: A stranger from the wreck sits by our fire and asks the way to the old kingdom.

focuses.name: Mending Old Quarrels
focuses.desc: The Speakers settle an old quarrel between the terraces and the harbour, and the island is calmer for it. Nobody quite remembers who first proposed the compromise.

then.tooltip: The stranger among us helped the Speakers settle them.

focuses.name: Honour His Choice
focuses.desc: The stranger will not stay to rule, and the Speakers do not ask him twice. They give him a boat, a chart and a blessing, and let him go.

focuses.name: The Road to Gala
focuses.desc: The islanders say that when the tales of men grow too old for any man to explain, they should be carried to Gala. The Speakers send a boat south with a keeper of tales.

effects.tooltip: When the tales of men grow too old for any man to explain, carry them to Gala.
